description_full: Amazon.com, Inc. engages in the retail sale of consumer products, advertising, and subscriptions service through online and physical stores in North America and internationally. The company operates through three segments: North America, International, and Amazon Web Services (AWS). It also manufactures and sells electronic devices, including Kindle, fire tablets, fire TVs, echo, ring, blink, and eero; and develops and produces media content. In addition, the company offers programs that enable sellers to sell their products in its stores; and programs that allow authors, independent publishers, musicians, filmmakers, Twitch streamers, skill and app developers, and others to publish and sell content. Further, it provides compute, storage, Artificial intelligence, database, analytics, machine learning, and other services, as well as advertising services through programs, such as sponsored ads, display, and video advertising. Additionally, the company offers Amazon Prime, a membership program. The company's products offered through its stores include merchandise and content purchased for resale and products offered by third-party sellers. It serves consumers, sellers, developers, enterprises, content creators, advertisers, and employees. The company was incorporated in 1994 and is headquartered in Seattle, Washington.

culture_narrative: Employs approximately 1.6M people. Revenue per employee of $438K ranks in the above the sector median among Consumer Cyclical peers, improving at 23%/yr — growing workforce leverage. Each employee generates $5K of free cash flow annually. Stock-based compensation of $12K per employee reflects an ownership culture. CEO compensation is 5× revenue per employee (modest relative to workforce productivity). Governance score flags elevated compensation governance risk (10/10).
financial_summary: Amazon.com, Inc. is a mega-cap consumer cyclical business with a $2.8T market cap on $716.9B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +12% over the past three years and +21% annually across the full decade, a respectable pace for a business of this size.

Returns on capital run at 21% against a 11% cost of capital — a 10-point spread that is the clearest signature of an economic moat, and 23% gross margins are typical of commodity economics where competitors can replicate the product cheaply.

The business throws off $7.7B in free cash flow — roughly 1 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.80× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year, and interest coverage of 35× is fortress-like.
Shareholder yield is only 0.0%, a thin return of capital, and insiders hold 8.8% of the shares.

sect: Its 11% operating margin is roughly in line with the Consumer Cyclical median (8%).
Its share of sector profits slightly exceeds its share of revenue (1.35x).
It accounts for 13.7% of sector revenue and 18.6% of sector operating profit.
Over five years it has been gaining share of the sector profit pool (+10.9% a year).
The sector is fragmented and competitive (HHI 0.03 across 377 companies in the universe; the top four hold 26% of revenue), so pricing power is hard to come by.
mkt: The shares have drifted higher, up 5% over the past year excluding the latest month.
The price sits mid-way through its 52-week range, 10% below the high.
With annualised volatility of 34% and a beta of 1.36, it amplifies market moves.
Liquidity is deep, with about $8.7B traded a day.
In past sell-offs it fell 23% in the 2020 crash, 52% in the 2022 bear market and 64% in 2008.
val: The price sits above its DCF fair value of $62.80 (margin of safety -313%), so there is no valuation cushion.
The fair-value models corroborate one another (dispersion 2%), and the Monte Carlo range runs $39.50 to $100 (P10-P90).
On multiples it looks expensive against Consumer Cyclical peers: EV/EBITDA 16.4 vs 11.2 and P/FCF 364.4 vs 16.5 (sector median).
Against its own history it is cheap: the EBIT multiple sits 50% below its 10-year median.
Earnings yields are thin: an FCF yield of 0.3% (below the risk-free rate) and an EBIT/EV of 2.7% (vs the 8% bar).
The 58 covering analysts target $327 on average, 26% above the price, well away from the model's fair value.
prof: ROIC of 21% clears the cost of capital of 11.3% by 10pp, the mark of a value creator; returns have swung a lot from year to year (CV 0.76).
It runs a 23% gross margin and converts 1% of revenue into free cash flow.
Earnings quality looks solid: cash conversion of 1.80x.
ROE of 19% comes mostly from margins and asset turnover rather than leverage (2.0x equity multiplier).
Operating margin is running 5pp above its own historical average, a peak-margin risk if conditions normalise.
It spends 2.7% of revenue on stock compensation (above the 2% gate).
hlth: The balance sheet carries net cash of $54.2B (2% of market cap).
It runs on negative working capital (-51 days), so customers and suppliers effectively fund its operations.
growth: Revenue has compounded at 11.7% over 3 years, 13.2% over 5 years and 21.0% over 10 years.
At current returns, reinvesting 100% of profits supports about 21.4% a year of fundamental growth, enough to sustain growth.
Free cash flow has compounded -21.6% a year over five years, short of the 5% durability bar.
Forward indicators: a book-to-bill of 1.04 and a backlog worth 11% of annual revenue.
Capex runs 2.0x depreciation (18.4% of sales), so it is building capacity for future growth.
Its Rule of 40 score is 12, below the 40 that marks a healthy growth business.
own: Insiders own 8.8%, meaningful skin in the game, and institutions hold 69%.
Insiders have only sold over the past year (21 sales, net $359.6M sold).
The share count has grown 1.2% a year over five years, diluting existing holders.
people: With about 1,638,000 employees, each generates about $438K of revenue, 1.2x the Consumer Cyclical median, and productivity has risen 23.5% a year.
That works out to $5K of free cash flow per employee.
The company is founder-led, which often keeps management aligned with long-term owners.
CEO pay is $2.1M (5x revenue per employee), and compensation governance scores poorly (10/10, lower is better).
